title: Show HN: Libretto – Making AI browser automations deterministic
description: A developer showcased Libretto, a tool for making AI browser automations deterministic, addressing reliability challenges in AI-powered web automation and testing workflows.
author: muchael

title: Ask HN: Who is using OpenClaw?
description: Hacker News discussion asking about real-world adoption and use cases for OpenClaw, revealing community interest and practical applications of autonomous AI agents in development workflows.
author: misterchocolat

title: Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS - Google's new text-to-speech model with prompt-based voice control
description: Google released Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS, a text-to-speech model that can be directed using detailed prompts. The prompting guide is surprisingly detailed, allowing control over accent, style, dynamics, pace, and even specific recording scenarios. Simon Willison tested it with different regional accents (Brixton, Newcastle, Exeter) and noted the results. He also used Gemini 3.1 Pro to 'vibe code' a UI for trying out the TTS functionality.
author: Simon Willison

title: Anthropic's rise is giving some OpenAI investors second thoughts
description: Investment analysis suggesting Anthropic's momentum is causing OpenAI investors to reconsider their positions, highlighting growing competition in the AI space and shifting market dynamics.
author: Connie Loizos

title: Anthropic co-founder confirms the company briefed the Trump administration on Mythos
description: Anthropic co-founder confirmed briefing the Trump administration on Mythos, indicating growing government interest in AI capabilities and potential regulatory engagement.
author: Sarah Perez

title: Google adds AI Skills to Chrome to help you save favorite workflows
description: Google introduced AI Skills in Chrome, allowing users to save AI prompts as repeatable workflows. This feature enables automation of common tasks and integration of AI assistance directly into the browser.
author: Sarah Perez

title: Google launches a Gemini AI app on Mac
description: Google released a Gemini app for macOS, allowing users to access Gemini from anywhere on their desktop and share windows. This marks Google's continued push to make Gemini more accessible across platforms.
author: Emma Roth

title: Adobe embraces conversational AI editing, marking a 'fundamental shift' in creative work
description: Adobe announced new conversational AI editing capabilities in Firefly, representing what they call a 'fundamental shift' in how creative professionals interact with AI tools for content creation.
author: Jess Weatherbed

title: Claude Code redesign focuses on managing multiple AI agents
description: Anthropic redesigned the Claude Code desktop app with new features for managing multiple AI agents simultaneously, including a sidebar for managing sessions, drag-and-drop workspace customization, and built-in terminal and file editor.
author: Stevie Bonifield

title: Gemini with Personal Intelligence is rolling out in more regions
description: Google's Personal Intelligence feature, which allows Gemini to access information from Gmail, Google Photos, Search, and YouTube watch history, is now rolling out globally (excluding UK, Switzerland, and EEA), starting with paid subscribers.
author: Emma Roth

title: Microsoft says its latest AI image model is a 'production workhorse'
description: Microsoft debuted MAI-Image-2-Efficient on Microsoft Foundry and MAI Playground, describing it as a faster, cheaper 'production workhorse' for businesses needing volume, speed, and cost control for product shots, marketing creatives, and UI mockups.
author: Tom Warren

title: Datasette CSRF protection modernization - Moving from tokens to Sec-Fetch-Site headers
description: Simon Willison landed a PR to replace Datasette's token-based CSRF protection with a modern approach using Sec-Fetch-Site headers, inspired by Go 1.25 and Filippo Valsorda's research. This removes the need for scattered CSRF tokens in templates and eliminates the skip_csrf plugin hook. Notably, Claude Code did much of the work across 10 commits, but Simon decided to write PR descriptions by hand to maintain honesty and conciseness.
author: Simon Willison

title: OpenAI's GPT-5.4-Cyber model and Trusted Access program
description: OpenAI announced GPT-5.4-Cyber, a 'cyber-permissive' variant fine-tuned for defensive cybersecurity use cases, along with their Trusted Access for Cyber program that allows users to verify identity via government ID to gain reduced friction access. Simon notes this appears to be OpenAI's answer to Anthropic's Claude Mythos and Project Glasswing. The announcement emphasizes OpenAI's years of cybersecurity work and goals to democratize access.
author: Simon Willison

title: Cybersecurity as Proof of Work - The economic implications of AI security testing
description: The UK's AI Safety Institute published an evaluation of Claude Mythos Preview's cyber capabilities. Drew Breunig notes that the more tokens (money) spent, the better the security results, leading to a concerning equation: 'to harden a system you need to spend more tokens discovering exploits than attackers will spend exploiting them.' This makes open source libraries more valuable since security tokens spent on them can be shared across all users.
author: Drew Breunig (covered by Simon Willison)

title: Google brings its Gemini Personal Intelligence feature to India
description: Google expanded Gemini Personal Intelligence to India, allowing the AI to access personal data from Gmail, Photos, Search, and YouTube to provide more contextualized assistance.
author: Ivan Mehta

title: Microsoft is working on yet another OpenClaw-like agent
description: Microsoft continues developing OpenClaw-like AI agents, signaling sustained investment in autonomous AI systems that can perform complex multi-step tasks with minimal human intervention.
author: Julie Bort

title: Microsoft is testing OpenClaw-like AI bots for Copilot
description: Microsoft is developing OpenClaw-like AI agents for its Copilot platform, continuing the trend of major tech companies building autonomous AI agents that can perform complex tasks.
author: The Verge Staff

title: SoftBank creates new company building 'physical AI'
description: SoftBank announced a new initiative to build AI models that can autonomously control machines and robots by 2030, with buy-in from Sony, Honda, and Nippon Steel. This represents a major push into 'physical AI' for robotics and autonomous systems.
author: Robert Hart

title: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch signals IPO readiness as AI agents fuel revenue surge
description: Vercel's CEO indicated the company is preparing for an IPO, driven by significant revenue growth from AI agent adoption. This highlights the commercial success and market demand for AI-powered developer tools.
author: Marina Temkin

title: Steve Yegge vs Google on AI adoption - Industry-wide 20/20/60 adoption curve
description: Steve Yegge claimed Google engineering has the same AI adoption footprint as John Deere (20% agentic power users, 20% refusers, 60% using chat tools). Google's Addy Osmani and Demis Hassabis strongly disputed this, noting over 40K SWEs use agentic coding weekly with access to internal tools. The debate highlights internal AI adoption challenges across the industry and the 18-month hiring freeze that may have prevented fresh perspectives.
author: Steve Yegge, Addy Osmani, Demis Hassabis

title: Exploring the new Servo crate - Embeddable browser engine for Rust
description: Following the April 2026 release of the servo v0.1.0 crate, Simon used Claude Code to explore what the embeddable browser engine can do. He built a CLI tool called 'servo-shot' for taking screenshots of URLs, which successfully rendered the Hacker News homepage. While compiling Servo to WebAssembly isn't feasible due to heavy thread usage, Claude built a playground for html5ever and markup5ever_rcdom crates.
author: Simon Willison

title: The peril of laziness lost - How LLMs lack the virtue of laziness
description: Bryan Cantrill argues that LLMs inherently lack the virtue of laziness - work costs nothing to an LLM, so they don't optimize for future time and will happily add layers of complexity. This highlights how essential human laziness is: our finite time forces us to develop crisp abstractions because we don't want to waste time dealing with clunky systems. Left unchecked, LLMs make systems larger, not better.
author: Bryan Cantrill (covered by Simon Willison)

title: The AI code wars are heating up
description: Analysis of how OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic are intensifying competition in AI-powered coding tools, with each major player vying for dominance in developer workflows and AI-assisted programming.
author: David Pierce

title: Audio transcription with Gemma 4 E2B using MLX
description: Simon shared a recipe for transcribing audio files on macOS using the 10.28 GB Gemma 4 E2B model with MLX and mlx-vlm. The 'uv run' command makes it easy to run transcription with various models. He tested it on a 14-second WAV file and found it worked well, with minor transcription errors due to audio quality.
author: Simon Willison

title: OpenAI responds to Axios HTTP hack by updating security certificates
description: After hackers compromised an Axios maintainer account and inserted malicious code affecting ChatGPT's macOS apps, OpenAI issued updates and new security certificates to mitigate risks to Windows, macOS, and Linux users.
author: Terrence O'Brien

title: Anthropic temporarily banned OpenClaw's creator from accessing Claude
description: Anthropic temporarily suspended OpenClaw's creator's access to Claude, raising questions about platform governance, API access policies, and tensions between AI platform providers and third-party tool developers.
author: Julie Bort

title: SQLite 3.53.0 release - ALTER TABLE constraints, JSON functions, and WebAssembly formatter
description: SQLite 3.53.0 is a significant release with ALTER TABLE support for adding/removing NOT NULL and CHECK constraints, new json_array_insert() function, and major CLI improvements including a new Query Results Formatter library. Simon used Claude Code on his phone to compile the formatter to WebAssembly and build a playground interface.
author: Simon Willison

title: Claude Cowork is ready to take over your company
description: Anthropic's Claude Cowork, a shared agentic AI workspace for macOS and Windows, added IT admin tools for company-wide deployments and new features including Zoom meeting transcript-to-action-items conversion. Available for paid organizational plans.
author: Thomas Ricker

title: The growing gap in AI capability based on access points - Voice mode vs Codex
description: Simon Willison noted that OpenAI's voice mode runs on a much older, weaker model (GPT-4o era with April 2024 cutoff), while the highest-tier paid Codex model can spend hours restructuring codebases or finding vulnerabilities. This insight was inspired by Andrej Karpathy's tweet about the growing gap in understanding AI capability based on access points. The difference stems from verifiable reward functions in coding and security domains, making them more amenable to RL training.
author: Simon Willison, Andrej Karpathy

title: ChatGPT has a new $100 per month Pro subscription
description: OpenAI launched a new $100/month ChatGPT Pro plan, representing a significant premium tier above existing offerings and targeting power users and businesses requiring intensive AI assistance.
author: The Verge Staff

title: ChatGPT finally offers $100/month Pro plan
description: OpenAI officially launched the $100/month ChatGPT Pro plan, positioning it as a premium tier for heavy users and enterprises requiring advanced AI capabilities and higher usage limits.
author: Julie Bort

title: Florida launches investigation into OpenAI
description: Florida Attorney General opened an investigation into OpenAI following a shooting incident that allegedly involved ChatGPT, raising new legal and regulatory scrutiny around AI safety and accountability.
author: The Verge Staff

title: The AI industry's race for profits is now existential
description: Analysis of how Anthropic and OpenAI are facing unprecedented pressure to achieve profitability, with 2026 emerging as a make-or-break year for major AI companies to demonstrate sustainable business models.
author: Nilay Patel

title: Is Anthropic limiting the release of Mythos to protect the internet — or Anthropic?
description: Analysis of Anthropic's cautious approach to Mythos release, exploring whether the strategy is motivated by safety concerns or competitive positioning in the AI landscape.
author: Tim Fernholz

title: Sierra's Bret Taylor says the era of clicking buttons is over
description: Sierra co-founder Bret Taylor declared that traditional UI interfaces are being replaced by AI-driven conversational interfaces, signaling a fundamental shift in how users interact with software.
author: Marina Temkin

title: PAL: Personal Adaptive Learner
description: Research paper introducing PAL, a Personal Adaptive Learner system that adapts to individual learning patterns and behaviors. Published April 15, 2026.
author: Megha Chakraborty, Darssan L. Eswaramoorthi, Madhur Thareja, et al.

title: Cycle-Consistent Search: Question Reconstructability as a Proxy Reward for Search Agent Training
description: Meta Superintelligence Labs researchers developed a new training method for search agents using question reconstructability as a proxy reward, improving agent performance in information retrieval tasks.
author: Sohyun An, Shuibenyang Yuan, Hayeon Lee, Cho-Jui Hsieh, Alexander Min

title: Drawing on Memory: Dual-Trace Encoding Improves Cross-Session Recall in LLM Agents
description: Research demonstrating that dual-trace encoding significantly improves memory recall across sessions in LLM-powered agents, addressing a key challenge in maintaining context and continuity for AI assistants.
author: Benjamin Stern, Peter Nadel

title: BEAM: Bi-level Memory-adaptive Algorithmic Evolution for LLM-Powered Heuristic Design
description: Introduction of BEAM, a bi-level memory-adaptive algorithm for LLM-powered heuristic design, enabling more efficient and adaptive AI systems for complex problem-solving.
author: Chuyang Xiang, Yichen Wei, Jiale Ma, et al.

title: GAM: Hierarchical Graph-based Agentic Memory for LLM Agents
description: Researchers developed GAM, a hierarchical graph-based memory system for LLM agents, improving information organization and retrieval in multi-agent systems with complex reasoning requirements.
author: Zhaofen Wu, Hanrong Zhang, Fulin Lin, et al.

title: Frontier-Eng: Benchmarking Self-Evolving Agents on Real-World Engineering Tasks
description: Introduction of Frontier-Eng, a benchmark for evaluating self-evolving AI agents on real-world engineering tasks, focusing on generative optimization and autonomous problem-solving capabilities.
author: Yizhe Chi, Deyao Hong, Dapeng Jiang, et al.

title: CIA: Inferring the Communication Topology from LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
description: Research presenting CIA, a method for inferring communication topology in LLM-based multi-agent systems, helping understand and optimize how AI agents coordinate and share information.
author: Yongxuan Wu, Xixun Lin, He Zhang, et al.
